commits.message:
feat: implement nested_storage_collections lint

Detect env.storage()....set() calls whose key or value type nests one
Soroban collection inside another (e.g. Map<Symbol, Map<u32, i128>> or
Map<Symbol, Vec<i128>>). Reading or writing such a value forces the host
to deserialize/re-serialize the whole nested structure even when only a
single inner element changes, so the lint suggests flattening with a
compound key (e.g. (Symbol, u32)) instead.

- Add NestedStorageCollections late lint pass plus is_soroban_collection/
  has_nested_soroban_collection helpers that inspect the generic type
  arguments of Map/Vec via typeck results.
- Add 1-level (non-flagged) and 2+-level (flagged) UI fixtures, including
  nesting in the storage key position and an #[allow] suppression case.
- Generalize the ui test's Map/Vec stubs to be generic over K/V so the
  new fixtures can express real nesting through the type system.
- Document the lint in docs/lints/nested_storage_collections.md, the
  README feature list, docs/lints/README.md, docs/cost_rationale.md, and
  CHANGELOG.md.

Closes #42

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' into feat/lint-nested-collections

# Conflicts:
#	soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr

fix: resolve CI build failures in SARIF output and fixture workspace

- SarifRun.results was typed Vec<SarifResult> while the SARIF result
  builder constructed plain serde_json::Value objects via json!(),
  a leftover mismatch from a prior merge that broke compilation.
  Retype results as Vec<serde_json::Value>, drop the now-dead typed
  Sarif* structs, and wire the already-collected rule descriptors
  into tool.driver.rules.
- integration.rs used HashSet<String> but inserted &str literals;
  fix the declared type.
- alpha/beta fixture crates each declared their own [workspace]
  while also being listed as members of the parent workspace,
  causing cargo metadata to fail with "multiple workspace roots
  found". Drop the redundant per-crate [workspace] tables.

These were the actual cause of the "SARIF result missing level"
CI failures reported on PRs #232, #267, #269, #270 (all inherited
the same broken merge state) — the binary failed to compile, it
was not a runtime field-mapping bug.
